sources.description: Note 9/9/2026: This dataset was updated in place to correct outstanding data issues, following our migration to a new asset management system in December 2024. You can access the previous version of the dataset here. A. SUMMARY This dataset contains all street trees recorded in the City’s street tree inventory. Each row represents a single street tree. The dataset is filtered from a broader asset inventory and includes only assets designated specifically as trees (excluding empty basins, landscaping areas, and potential planting sites). It does not include Street Trees that have been removed. You can find most trees that have been removed in the Street Tree Removal Notifications dataset. B. HOW THE DATASET IS CREATED The dataset is extracted from the Public Works asset management system (CMMS) and filtered to include only assets classified as street trees. Non‑tree assets such as empty basins, landscaping areas, and potential planting sites are excluded to ensure each record represents a single street tree. C. UPDATE PROCESS The dataset is updated on a daily basis by automatically extracting the latest street tree records from the Public Works asset management system. D. HOW TO USE THIS DATASET Not all street trees in the dataset have coordinates; for records that do include coordinates, the precision may vary, so users should review spatial accuracy before performing location‑based analysis. Tree information is updated as part of normal operational workflows: typically when inspectors or field staff interact with a tree for maintenance, inspection, or other actions. As a result, while the dataset is refreshed on a scheduled basis, individual tree records may not always reflect the most current conditions. Please note that trees removed on an emergency basis (e.g. storm or life hazard) may not appear in this dataset or in the Street Trees Removal Notifications dataset. The Street Trees Removal Notifications dataset is only for the formal removal process where a tree removal permit is issued and the tree was recommended for removal. E. RELATED DATASETS Street Tree Removal Notifications

A. SUMMARY Street Tree Removal public notifications managed by San Francisco Public Works. B. HOW THE DATASET IS CREATED Data is based on 24-hour, 15-day, or 30-day public notices posted on the trees after a Street Tree Removal Permit was issued by the City. C. UPDATE PROCESS Updated daily. D. HOW TO USE THIS DATASET Each record is a street tree removal public notice after a permit was issued and the tree was recommended for removal.

limitations: This is a current inventory, not a complete historical census. Missing planting dates do not imply recent trees.
The archived inventory contains historical removals, non-tree sites, and duplicates. It is never added to the current population.
Legacy DBH is an undated archived observation. It must not be used to calculate growth rates.
Removal notifications document permits and notices, not verified completion dates. Emergency removals may be absent.
The inventory publishes no per-tree health assessments, measured height, crown spread, inspection reports, pruning dates, or full maintenance schedules.
A timeline filtered by known planting date is a recorded-planting cohort among current trees, not a reconstruction of the forest at a past date.
Coordinates can be missing or imprecise. Species identification and record conditions have not been independently field verified.
The current source retains some stump, paved-over, landscape, and planting-site labels despite its stated tree-only scope. These records are preserved and flagged, not silently removed.
A small number of source planting dates are in the future; these must not be interpreted as an observed completed planting or a negative age.
Species traits, rendered specimens, and Street View imagery require separate attribution and are not observations of an individual tree.
